title: Focus velocity heatmap notes
body:
Purpose: quick personal checkpoint for the 2-week cadence. Use as scratchpad to track where attention actually went vs planned, and a compact OKR draft for the next cycle.

Summary snapshot:
- Week range: 2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-15 (two-week block I'm reflecting on)
- Main focus: reduce tail latency variance for small-batch interactive API (latency SLOs), unblock a rollout, and keep personal learning time for quantization reading.
- Signal: felt most productive mornings (9:00–12:00), deep work <3x sessions this cycle. Meetings ate the afternoons.

Heatmap (hours of focused work/day, rough):
Mon  Tue  Wed  Thu  Fri  Sat  Sun
 3    1.5   2.5   1     2    1.5   0.5
Mon2 Tue2 Wed2 Thu2 Fri2 Sat2 Sun2
 2    2     3     1.5   1    0.5   0.5

Interpretation: two concentrated mid-week deep days (Wed/Wed2). Split across sprint tasks produced 60% progress on the rollout checklist but not enough to finish the canary plan.

Personal KPI / micro-OKR draft for next 2-week block (for personal tracking, not formal OKR):
Objective: Close the rolling canary and reduce 95th percentile token latency for small-batch chat by 20%.
- KR1: Implement KV cache hot-path fix and validate end-to-end in staging (target: end of week 1).
- KR2: Produce a synthetic load test demonstrating 20% reduction in p95 for 1-2 token bursts (target: run by day 10).
- KR3: Document rollout runbook and get 2 engineers to approve (target: day 12).
- Personal KR4 (learning): Read & summarize 3 papers on attention-kernel approximations and note practical ops tradeoffs (timebox: 4 hours).

Signals to watch (metrics + qualitative):
- System: p95 token latency for small batch (1–4 requests) and tail error rate for canary.
- Cost: token/second delta after cache fix (should be neutral or improve).
- Human: number of context-switch interruptions >30m per day (goal: keep <=1).

Retro: what went well
- Grew a short checklist that helped me triage propagation issues faster.
- Two small experiments (prefetching emboss) yielded measurable decrease in repeated token generation cost.

Retro: what didn't go well
- Afternoon meetings fragmented deep work; lost momentum on day-of-runbook writing.
- I underestimated infra flakiness (staging gpu preemptions blocked a 2-hour validation).
- My PR review queue backlog slowed approvals by ~36 hours average.

Ideas / experiments for next block
- Reserve two contiguous 3-hour deep-blocks on calendar each week and mark as Do-Not-Disturb; communicate to team as my focused dev hours.
- Set a pre-checklist for canary runs to reduce staging flakiness (small automations: env-health-check, node-availability check).
- Move learning hour to first thing in week to guarantee completion.

Open questions / risks
- If p95 improvement is under 10% after KV changes, do we revert to batching changes? (Decision fork: more infra work vs model-variant fallback).
- Are SREs comfortable with the proposed canary automation? Need an alignment sync.

Next actions (concrete)
- Day 1: carve two deep blocks in calendar + post update in #serving-runtime about my deep hours. (Jonah to review calendar wording)
- Day 2–4: implement staging pre-check hook + small script to assert node health before canary. (allocate 3–4 hours)
- Day 5: open PR for KV hot-path fix; ping Maya for early review.
- Day 7: run synthetic p95 test and capture results (script + runbook).
- Day 10–12: finalize runbook + obtain 2 approvals.

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep the learning KR small: 3 papers not 5. Summaries should be 200–300 words each (one-paragraph practical takeaways).
- Consider short-term fallback: advertise a model-variant with quantized profile for high-latency times (ops cost vs perf tradeoff).

Slack/jira/link references (quick):
- Slack threads: #serving-runtime "canary plan" (link pinned)
- JIRA: PLAT-843 (canary pipeline), PLAT-912 (kv-hot-path bug)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1123 (early KV change)

End-of-block micro-retro template (to copy next time):
- snapshot metrics (p95/p50/errors), time heatmap, 3 wins, 3 blockers, 3 next actions, 1 learning note.

Scratch end.
short_summary: Two-week personal scratchpad with a focus-velocity heatmap, micro-OKR draft to close a canary rollout and reduce p95 latency, retro notes, concrete next actions, and open questions.
